decisions.reason: As a reusable agricultural crate it fits the firm's sustainability and logistics offering, and despite only modest website prominence management can still attribute any weaker uptake to crop-cycle and customer adoption timing after having already invested in launch.

The foldable large container received the strongest public commitment with its own page in both observed years and sits very close to the firm's core returnable packaging strategy, so management is likely to persist.
A stackable plastic crate is a highly standard, central product for a reusable packaging maker, making it easy for management to justify continued support even without heavy standalone promotion.
The medium-duty rackable pallet extends the core pallet range and uses existing manufacturing and customer relationships, so sunk development and portfolio logic favor retention.

The spill-retention pallet appears less central to the firm's main returnable transport packaging direction and lost website prominence after launch, making it the easiest product for management to discontinue despite prior investment.

Although its visibility fell after launch, the plastic pallet with load retainers remains a close adjaceny to the firm's core pallet business, so escalation of commitment and platform reuse still tilt management toward keeping it.
